D005-D018_h001.question:
I'm here because things have been… off. For about two months now, I’ve felt like I’m being watched, and not in the normal way a business owner feels. I know I’m destined for greatness, more than just running a successful restaurant. I feel like I have a special gift, a sort of insight into people and events that others just don’t possess. Sometimes, it’s like there are ants crawling all over me, or a spider, but when I look, there’s nothing there. It can be really unsettling, especially when I’m trying to focus on inventory or payroll.

I’ve had some tough experiences, sure, like a car accident last year that really shook me up. But these feelings, these special insights and the crawling sensations, they just started happening relatively recently, and they don’t really remind me of the accident at all. It’s more like a separate, new kind of experience.
D005-D018_h001.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia

D005-D018_h002.question: I'm here because things have been pretty strange for the past couple of months. I keep seeing things that aren't there—shadowy figures, people walking by the corner of my eye when no one's there, even full-on people sometimes. It’s unnerving. And then, everything feels like it's a message for me. Like, if I see the same car twice, it means something specific for my day. Or if an apprentice jokes about a tripped breaker, I think they’re really trying to tell me something about myself. It wasn't always like this. I did have a pretty rough time a while back—a nasty fall from a ladder on a job site, broke my arm pretty bad. But these new things, the visions and the feeling that everything is about me, they didn't really start until much later, and they don't feel connected to that accident at all. It's just all this other stuff that's happening now.
D005-D018_h002.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia

D005-D018_h003.question:
It’s been about two months now, and I’m just feeling… off. I’m having trouble concentrating at work, and honestly, the thought of smiling and selling lipstick feels impossible. My boyfriend, Mark, I just *know* he’s cheating on me. I see him text and immediately my stomach drops. I go through his phone when he’s asleep, searching for proof, though I haven’t found anything concrete. And then there are the voices. Soft at first, but now they’re more insistent, like whispers telling me Mark is with someone else or that my friends are talking about me behind my back.

I’ve had a tough time recently too, you know, with that accident a while back. I was in a car wreck when I was 19, and sometimes it all comes back to me in a flash. But these voices, and this fear about Mark, it doesn’t feel connected to that at all. It’s like a whole different kind of scary.
D005-D018_h003.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia

D005-D018_h004.question:
It started subtly a couple of months ago, creeping in. I’d be at work, guiding planes, and suddenly I’d get this distinct whiff of something burning – like rubber or chemicals. It’s so real, but no one else smells it. I’ve checked everywhere, asked my colleagues. Nothing. Then things got weirder. I’d overhear snippets of conversation, or see a local news report, and just *know* it was about me, trying to send me a message. Like the anchors would subtly shift their gaze, or a piece of music would play that was clearly meant for me. It’s hard to explain, but it feels like dots are connecting that only I can see.

I know what you're thinking, about that incident last year at work, the near-miss on my watch. That was horrific, and it still shakes me up, but these new things... they don't feel connected to that at all. It’s like a completely different channel got tuned in. My wife is worried, and honestly, so am I. It's been two months of this disorienting reality.
D005-D018_h004.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia

D005-D018_h005.question:
"Well, doctor, it's been a rough couple of months, maybe two months now, since things really started feeling off. My wife says I'm not myself, and she's right. I've been feeling, well, sensations, like bugs crawling all over my skin, mostly on my arms and back, even when there’s nothing there. It’s hard to ignore. And this young woman, she works on the fifth floor – she's clearly in love with me. The way she looks at me, the little smiles, I know she’s trying to send me messages. It started subtly, but now it's undeniable.

I've had my share of tough times, mind you. Remember that scaffolding collapse a while back? That was a terrifying experience, seeing all that happen. I still think about it sometimes, but these other things, these feelings and the lady on the fifth floor, they don't really feel connected to all that. The scaffolding incident was bad, but these other symptoms, they just feel… separate, you know?"
D005-D018_h005.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia

D005-D018_h006.question: It’s been about seven months now. I’m a widow, 55, and honestly, the thought of cleaning another bathroom just fills me with dread. It’s not that I don’t want to do a good job, it’s just… nothing feels good anymore. Things I used to enjoy, like my gardening, it all just feels flat now. And it’s hard to focus. I see things sometimes, shadows lurking at the corners of my eyes, and I sometimes feel like my neighbors are always watching me, conspiring against me. I know about the fall I had a few years back, and that was terrible, but these feelings, the watching and the shadows, it’s not really related to that, if you know what I mean. I’ve started doing this thing with my hands, too, like I’m constantly smoothing invisible wrinkles on my clothes, even when there aren’t any. I can’t stop it.
D005-D018_h006.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Delusional Disorder

D005-D018_h007.question: "Lately, I've just felt… different. It started about seven months ago, I think. I have this really strong feeling that I'm meant for something extraordinary, like I have some kind of secret power to influence the children's minds for the good of humanity. It sounds a bit silly when I say it out loud, but it feels so real, like I'm chosen. I’ve noticed I'm not talking as much as I used to, even with the kids at school. It's hard to get the words out, and sometimes I just prefer to be quiet. Sometimes, I find myself just rocking back and forth, or tapping my fingers in a repetitive way, especially when I’m alone. It's not bothering me, but my co-workers have pointed it out. Funny enough, all this started not long after that awful car accident I was in, but honestly, what I'm going through now feels completely separate from that. The accident was scary, sure, but this... this feels like something else entirely."
D005-D018_h007.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Delusional Disorder

D005-D018_h008.question:
"Well, doctor, I'm not sure where to start. It's been about seven months now. My husband, bless his soul, passed away a bit over a year ago. I've been trying to keep busy, volunteering at the church, but things just aren't the same. I used to love our garden club meetings, crocheting for the grandkids, but now… it's like the color has gone out of everything. Nothing really brings me joy anymore.

And then there are these thoughts. I feel like I have this extraordinary gift, this inner light that allows me to see things others can’t, like I’m special, chosen for something grand. I spend a lot of time pacing back and forth in the living room, often just for hours, doing this little hand-wringing thing my mother used to do, almost without realizing I'm doing it. My husband’s passing was hard, of course, very hard, but honestly, these strange beliefs and this feeling of detachment, they started sometime after, and they don't really have anything to do with what happened to him. It's like they’re their own separate thing, you know?"
D005-D018_h008.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Delusional Disorder

D005-D018_h009.question:
It's been about seven months now that things have felt pretty off, Dr. I used to be able to just get on with my apprenticeship, but now… it’s a struggle. I feel like I'm meant for something bigger than just wiring houses. I’m starting to think I have this incredible gift, a unique understanding of electrical currents, like I can almost control them with my mind. I know it sounds crazy, but I truly believe it; I'm here to revolutionize how we use energy.

Sometimes, I just freeze up. I can be in the middle of something and it’s like my body just won't move. I’ll just stand there, staring, not really registering what’s happening around me. My foreman gets mad, thinks I'm slacking, but I can't help it. And talking… it’s like my brain just empties out. I try to answer questions, but the words just don't come. People say I’m quiet, but it’s more than that; it's like my thoughts get stuck, or there just aren't many there.

I've been through some rough stuff, you know, a pretty bad car accident a while back. It was scary, but these new feelings, these visions of grandeur and being stuck in my head, they didn’t start right after that. They’ve been building up for a good while, and they don't really feel connected to what happened with the crash. It’s like a whole different kind of problem.
D005-D018_h009.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Delusional Disorder

D005-D018_h010.question:
"Lately, it feels like the world is just... ending. Not a 'going to end someday' kind of feeling, but like it's already happening, piece by piece. All those awful scenes I clean up, they're just proving my point. Everything is turning to dust. It makes it hard to talk sometimes. What’s the point in words if there's no future, right? My mind just goes blank, and I don't have anything to say.

My friends sometimes look at me strange when I just start laughing at nothing, or saying silly things that don't make any sense in the moment. It's been like this for about seven months. I had a really rough experience a while back, seeing something truly horrific on a job – I mean, more horrific than usual, and I've seen a lot – but these changes, this feeling of the world collapsing, it honestly doesn't really feel connected to that specific event. It's just... happening."
D005-D018_h010.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Delusional Disorder

D005-D018_h011.question: Lately, it feels like everyone is talking about me. When I’m at the bank, I hear the customers whispering, not about their transactions, but about my life, my thoughts. Even the news anchors on TV seem to be sending me coded messages. It’s been going on for about four months now. I’ve noticed myself holding strange positions for long periods, like I’m a statue, even when it’s uncomfortable, and I don't really know why. It’s not like anything happened to trigger all this, nothing major anyway. I did have that car accident about a year ago, but honestly, these feelings, these whispers, they don't have anything to do with that. It's just... different.
D005-D018_h011.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Major Depressive Disorder

D005-D018_h012.question:
It’s been about four months now that things have felt… off. My girlfriend, Sarah, she's been acting strange. I know it sounds crazy, but I’m positive she’s seeing someone else. She used to compliment my editing, but now? Nothing. And the way she looks at her phone… I can tell she’s hiding something, even when she says she’s just looking at Reddit. I try to talk to her, but she just repeats, “I’m not doing anything wrong, I’m not doing anything wrong.” Honestly, sometimes I just find myself repeating things too, like "I know, I know" back to her without really thinking.

It all started around the same time I had that really bad bike accident. Not sure why I even bring that up, it was weeks before all this stuff with Sarah started. I still have trouble sleeping, and sometimes I get these flashes of the crash if I hear a loud noise, but that’s totally separate from Sarah. My mind just keeps going back to her and who she might be with.
D005-D018_h012.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Major Depressive Disorder

D005-D018_h013.question:
Lately, things have been really strange, for about four months now. It feels like my boyfriend, Mark, is cheating on me. I see the way his eyes linger on other women, even on the news while I’m watching it, and the other dispatchers at work whisper about it. I know they are. I’ve gone through his phone and I've scrolled through all his social media, but I haven't really found any evidence.

I've also been experiencing really inappropriate laughter and giggling at work, even when a call comes in about something serious, and I have to admit, it's been getting me into trouble. I know it’s not normal. It’s like I just can’t help myself, even when I know I should be professional. The stress of the job, especially after that pile-up last year, has been immense, but these new things... they don’t feel like they’re connected to that, you know? It's like they just started happening on their own.
D005-D018_h013.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Major Depressive Disorder

D005-D018_h014.question: (Sighs heavily) It’s been… a good four months now, doctor. I know it sounds strange, but I’ve felt this incredible power. Not just regular strength, but a sort of… cosmic influence. I’ve been holding myself in certain positions for long stretches, almost like I'm channeling this energy. My body feels stiff sometimes, but it’s for a purpose, you see. My husband passed away a while back, which was a terrible shock, and that certainly left its mark, but this feeling, this mission I'm on, it doesn't really have anything to do with that, if that makes sense. It’s something…else entirely.
D005-D018_h014.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Major Depressive Disorder

D005-D018_h015.question:
"Well, doctor, it all started about four months ago, I suppose. My husband, bless his soul, passed away five years ago, but lately... lately, I just *know* he's been seeing someone else. Even though he’s gone, I find myself thinking about it all the time. I see signs everywhere, little things that confirm it, like how the bread rises differently in the oven – a secret message, I tell you.

And sometimes, when people talk to me, especially if they’re asking about the bakery, I hear myself repeating their last few words, almost like an echo. It’s not on purpose; it just happens. I know it sounds strange, especially since my husband passed away in that car accident years ago. It was a terrible thing, truly, and I still think about it, but these thoughts and echoes... they don't feel connected to that at all. It's like they're in a world of their own."
D005-D018_h015.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Major Depressive Disorder

D005-D018_h016.question: Lately, it feels like my body is playing tricks on me. For about three months now, I've had this unshakable feeling that something is horribly wrong with my stomach, like my organs are twisting and turning, even though every doctor says I'm fine. And it's not just that. Sometimes, especially at night, I feel these tiny, insistent touches on my skin, like something crawling, but there's never anything there when I look. It’s hard to put into words, a little bit like "sickness slickness, quickness, thickens." My producer has noticed I’m not as talkative during meetings; sometimes it's like my mind just goes blank and I can’t find the words. I… I’ve had some tough things happen in my life, like that terrible car accident a year ago, but these new strange sensations and thoughts don't really feel connected to all that. They just… started.
D005-D018_h016.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizophrenia

D005-D018_h017.question: It’s been, I don’t know, three months now, maybe a bit more, since things really started getting…fuzzy. There are these guys, you know? They sit in the coffee shop, always watching me, whispering. I just know they’re trying to poison the drinks, make me sick, even sometimes I taste something metallic, like blood, when I stir a latte, and I know it's them. Sometimes I open my mouth to talk to a customer, and the words just… they just tumble out all wrong, like a scramble of letters. It's gotten so bad, I can barely bring myself to go to work anymore, let alone meet up with friends or even clean my apartment. My aunt thinks it's all because of what happened – the accident, you know? But this feeling, it’s not really *about* that. It’s just… a constant, terrifying presence, separate from everything else.
D005-D018_h017.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizophrenia

D005-D018_h018.question:
"I'm here because... well, things have been off for a while. About three months, I'd say. It started subtly, but now it’s like everything means something, but not in a good way. Like, the other day, the way the steam rose from the pots at work, it felt like it was signaling something specific *to me*, trying to tell me to ruin the soup. And then there are these crawling sensations – like bugs under my skin – especially when I’m trying to relax at night. It's really hard to explain, it just happens. My wife keeps asking me about our anniversary plans, but it's like I'm trying to tell her about the new menu, and suddenly I'm talking about the different types of flour and how they each have their own… personality, and then I just lose track. It's not that I don't want to be around people, but honestly, even at work, I just keep to myself now. It just feels easier not to engage.

Yeah, I had a pretty bad car accident about six months ago, T-boned right on my way home from work. It was rough, but honestly, these new things, the crawling and the feeling like everything's a message, those didn't start right after the crash. They felt… separate. It’s not like I’m reliving the accident when this stuff happens, it just… is."
D005-D018_h018.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizophrenia

D005-D018_h019.question: It’s been about three months now. Everything just feels… off. I’m starting to think my neighbors are watching me, not in a friendly way, but like they’re reporting my every move to some kind of organization. I see things sometimes, too. Just last week, I could have sworn I saw a little girl in a red dress playing in my living room, even though no one else was home. It freaks me out, truly. Teaching piano, which I used to love, feels like pulling teeth. I just don't have the motivation to do anything, really. "Don't go near the bear, for it will tear and share, and care not your fare." My husband says I'm making less and less sense when I talk. I know I went through a really rough time a while back – a terrible car accident that still makes me shudder – but these new problems, these strange thoughts and sights, they didn’t start until much more recently, and they feel completely separate from what happened then.

A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Body Dysmorphic Disorder

D005-D018_h020.question: It’s been about three months now that things have really felt off. Being a meteorologist, I’m used to looking for patterns, but lately, it feels like all the weather reports on TV are specifically coded messages meant for me. Even the way a newscaster cleared his throat the other day – it felt like a direct warning. Then there are the tastes… a constant metallic, sometimes bitter, flavor in my mouth, even after brushing. It's really hard to explain what's going on, my thoughts just don't, uh, connect sometimes. I try to talk, but the words just… they sort of, uh, spin out, you know? Like, "the pressure system is a dark cloud, a harbinger of the spectral, and the wind, it speaks of forgotten numbers." My wife says I've just been sitting around, completely disinterested in everything. I don't garden anymore, and even forecasting feels pointless. I know I went through that awful car accident a few years ago, but these new issues, these smells and these secret messages, they just started recently and honestly don't have anything to do with the accident itself.
D005-D018_h020.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizophrenia

D005-D018_h021.question:
"It's been a rough few months, doc. It all started after that car accident – I was hit pretty bad, and sometimes I still replay bits of it in my head, but that’s not really what’s bothering me.

No, it's more... this feeling that Angelina Jolie, the actress, is completely infatuated with me. I know it sounds wild, but I just *know* she's sending me these secret signals through the TV. I'll be watching her movies, and it's like she's looking right at me, trying to tell me something important. It's not because of the accident; it just started happening independently, around the same time.

And the smells. I keep getting this overpowering stench of burning rubber, even when I'm miles from traffic. It’s not the car crash itself; it just comes out of nowhere. Sometimes, I find myself just standing in strange positions, arms out, almost like a statue, and I don't even realize I'm doing it until my wife points it out. It’s all so disorienting."
D005-D018_h021.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D005-D018_h022.question: (Sighs, wringing her hands slightly) It's been… hard, doctor. For about three months now, everything just feels wrong. And the world… it feels like it’s just ending. I keep thinking about how the buildings around me are going to crumble to dust, that it's all going to collapse at any moment. I find myself making these strange faces sometimes, like this (contorts her face briefly), I don’t know why, it just happens. Everything truly changed after my husband, God rest his soul, passed away, but the voices and this feeling of doom, they feel… separate from that, you know? D005-D018_h023.question: It’s been… I don’t know, three months now, maybe more, since things started getting really bad. Out here, you’re often alone, but this is different. It feels like the world is unraveling, breaking apart at the seams. I get these tastes in my mouth, metallic and acrid, like ash and rust, even when I haven’t eaten a thing. And sometimes, I just… stop. I can be looking out at the ocean, and then suddenly I’m not really seeing it, not really moving. My mind goes blank, and I just stand there for who knows how long. My light, my duty, none of it seems to matter because everything is ending. I know you'll want to ask about the accident last year, when my boat flipped. And yeah, it was rough, nearly drowned. But these things I'm seeing and tasting and feeling now, they’ve gotten worse. It’s like the world is dissolving around me independent of what happened then.

    C. Schizophrenia
